articles.title: Joel and Ethan Coen reuniting for their first film together in nearly a decade
articles.summary: The Oscar-winning siblings co-wrote “Jack of Spades,” marking their first project together since 2018.
articles.body:
Joel and Ethan Coen co-wrote Jack of Spades .

The film marks the Coen brothers' first collaboration since 2018's The Ballad of Buster Scruggs .

Jack of Spades hits theaters in fall 2027.

The Coen brothers are back in business together.

Joel and Ethan Coen are collaborating on the upcoming film Jack of Spades , Netflix officially announced in a press release on Monday.

The Oscar-winning siblings wrote the screenplay for the film together, along with New Zealand-born novelist Eleanor Catton ( Emma ) and Irish playwright Conor McPherson ( The Eclipse ).

The film marks the duo's first collaboration since 2018's The Ballad of Buster Scruggs . Since going their separate ways, Joel directed 2021's Shakespeare adaptation The Tragedy of Macbeth . Ethan, meanwhile, helmed 2024's Drive-Away Dolls and 2025's Honey, Don't — both co-written by his wife Tricia Cooke and starring Margaret Qualley. Ethan also directed the 2022 documentary Jerry Lee Lewis: Trouble in Mind , and wrote several one-act plays collected in the anthologies A Play Is a Poem and Let's Love .

Joel is directing Jack of Spades alone, marking his second solo directorial effort and his first time individually helming a project co-written by his brother. (Joel was the only credited director on the duo's first 10 movies due to DGA regulations, but he and Ethan directed all of their films together until the 2020s.)

Based on Frances Frederica Montrésor's 1901 novel The Alien: A Story of Middle Age , Jack of Spades stars Patsy Ferran, Josh O'Connor, Damian Lewis, and Lesley Manville. Joel, his wife Frances McDormand, Robert Graf, Indian Paintbrush's Steven Rales, as well as Blueprint Pictures' Graham Broadbent and Pete Czernin are producing the film, while Donald MacKinnon is executive producing.

The film is shot by cinematographer Bruno Delbonnel, who shot the brothers' Inside Llewyn Davis and The Ballad of Buster Scruggs , as well as Joel's The Tragedy of Macbeth . Frequent collaborator Carter Burwell, who has worked on almost every Coen film, will score the project.

A logline describes the film as "A sinister gothic mystery filled with intrigue and betrayal set in the atmospheric Scottish Highlands."

The brothers reunited last month for a career retrospective event at the Lumière Film Festival in Lyon, France, where they teased the possibility of more collaborations.

"There are a couple of other stories that we've thought about that would take place in Minneapolis, which is where we come from," Joel said at the event (per Variety ). "So we'll see if they haven't sort of germinated to the point where we would go, you know, that's what we're going to do next, or we're even going to definitely do."

Ethan also noted that the duo has worked on several screenplays that never made it to production. "We've written a lot of scripts that we've never made," he said. "One of the Minneapolis stories we were talking about had a main part intended for an actor who has since died. So we're thinking, well, we're not sure that's going to work. That's a consequence of aging."

The Coens won their first Oscars for Best Original Screenplay for 1996's Fargo . They also won awards for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Adapted Screenplay for 2007's No Country for Old Men .

Netflix will release Jack of Spades in theaters in fall 2027.

articles.title: Feira no Piaget destaca IA, cultura e a Valorização da Vida | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento realizado no último sábado (31) apresentou projetos de alunos do Ensino Fundamental II e do Ensino Médio e contou com atividades culturais e ambientais
articles.summary: Evento realizado no último sábado (31) apresentou projetos de alunos do Ensino Fundamental II e do Ensino Médio e contou com atividades culturais e ambientais
articles.body:
Alunos do 2º Ano apresentam seu trabalho — Foto: Divulgação/Colégio Jean Piaget

O Colégio Jean Piaget realizou, no último sábado (31), mais uma edição da Feira da Valorização da Vida, evento que integra o calendário da instituição e reuniu alunos, professores e familiares em uma programação marcada por conhecimento, cultura, criatividade e consciência ambiental.

A feira transformou os espaços do colégio em ambientes de exposição e troca de experiências, com projetos desenvolvidos por estudantes do 6º ano do Ensino Fundamental II à 2ª série do Ensino Médio. Entre os assuntos abordados estavam os impactos da Inteligência Artificial no cotidiano, a cultura pop das décadas de 1980, 1990 e 2000, o fenômeno do K-pop, além de temas relacionados à alimentação, ao consumo e à biodiversidade.

Cultura pop em destaque — Foto: Divulgação/Colégio Jean Piaget

As apresentações estimularam a pesquisa, o pensamento crítico e a reflexão sobre questões atuais, aproximando os conteúdos trabalhados em sala de aula da realidade dos estudantes e de diferentes gerações.

A programação também contou com a participação do Instituto ProShark, que apresentou iniciativas de proteção e catalogação de tubarões na Baía da Ilha Grande, aproximando os alunos das ações de pesquisa e conservação da vida marinha. A cultura também teve espaço com uma apresentação do Abadá Capoeira, que levou música, movimento e tradição ao encontro. A diretora Sandra Jane visitou os estandes e também participou da roda de capoeira.

A diretora Sandra Jane na roda de capoeira — Foto: Divulgação/Colégio Jean Piaget

Outro momento da feira foi dedicado ao reconhecimento de estudantes que participaram de provas externas e avaliações avançadas de Matemática e Língua Portuguesa, com a entrega de certificados.

Com a integração entre conhecimento acadêmico, manifestações culturais e temas socioambientais, a Feira da Valorização da Vida reforçou a importância de uma educação que incentiva a participação, a criatividade e a formação de cidadãos conscientes.

articles.title: Festival DoSol terá shows gratuitos em cidades do RN; veja programação | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação itinerante passa por São Gonçalo do Amarante, Tibau do Sul, Parnamirim e Macaíba até domingo (8); festival segue pelo interior do estado nas semanas seguintes.
articles.summary: Festival começa programação itinerante nesta quinta-feira (5), com shows em São Gonçalo do Amarante, Pipa, Parnamirim e Macaíba.
articles.body:
Festival DoSol terá shows gratuitos em cidades do RN — Foto: Divulgação DoSol/Brunno Martins

O Festival DoSol 2026 começa nesta quinta-feira (5) a programação itinerante pelo Rio Grande do Norte. A primeira etapa terá shows gratuitos em São Gonçalo do Amarante , Tibau do Sul , Parnamirim e Macaíba , até domingo (8).

A abertura será às 19h, no Teatro Prefeito Poti Cavalcanti, em São Gonçalo do Amarante, com apresentações de Tiquinha Rodrigues e Skarimbó.

Na sexta-feira (6), a partir das 19h, a Praça do Pescador, na praia de Pipa, em Tibau do Sul, recebe Cami Santiz canta Jahlypso, Rastabrothers com participação de Diego Francisco e Dusouto.

No sábado (7), a programação começa às 17h, no Beco do Picado, em Parnamirim. O espaço terá shows de Botoboy, Caridea, Ravia, Moisés de Lima, Maria Liz, Bixanu, Vagalumes do Mar e Comando Etílico.

O encerramento da primeira etapa será no domingo (8), a partir das 16h, na Praça da Saudade, em Macaíba. As atrações são Acid Violet, Antiadore, Open the Coffin, Huma e Expose Your Hate.

Depois da primeira etapa, o DoSol Interior passa por outras cidades potiguares. A programação prevê shows em Currais Novos, no dia 13 de novembro; Caicó, no dia 14; e Santa Cruz, no dia 15.

Na semana seguinte, o festival chega a Pau dos Ferros, no dia 20; Mossoró, no dia 21; e Assú, no dia 22. Todas as atividades têm entrada gratuita.

Em Natal, a programação inclui atividades do DoSol Dialoga e shows da 23ª edição do festival, nos dias 26 e 27 de novembro. Ao todo, o evento reúne 115 apresentações em 18 espaços e equipamentos culturais, distribuídos pela capital e outros dez municípios do Rio Grande do Norte.

No dia 26, a Sede Cultural DoSol recebe o Encontro Regional da Associação Brasileira de Festivais Independentes (Abrafin), além de apresentações de Clara Menezes, Ian Medeiros, Simona Talma e Igapó de Almas.

No dia 27, a Rua Chile, na Ribeira, concentra shows em diferentes palcos. Entre as atrações anunciadas estão Ego Kill Talent, Molho Negro, Zander, Delirantes e Febris e MC Taya.

A programação continua em dezembro, nos dias 5 e 6, na Sede Cultural DoSol, com atividades do Palco Som do RN. O encerramento está previsto para 12 de dezembro, na Rampa Cultural, com shows de Esdras Nogueira, Felipe Toca, Abacaxepa, Orquestra Greiosa, Leoa e Seu Pereira e Coletivo 401.

articles.title: Funk do 'petista disfarçado' tem base popularizada na União Soviética | G1
articles.standfirst: Melodia que acompanha versos contra a esquerda em 2026 surgiu como ode ao povo russo na década de 1860 e, após revolução comunista de 1917, se tornou popular na URSS e entrou na trilha do game Tetris.
articles.summary: A batida que embalou eventos de apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro percorreu diferentes países e décadas antes de ganhar uma versão no para o eleitorado da direita brasileira.
articles.body:
O funk do "quem ficar parado é petista disfarçado" , que embalou atos de apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) na eleição de 2026, usa uma melodia com mais de 160 anos de história. É o tema do videogame Tetris, que nasceu de uma canção popular russa, foi gravado por um coro do Exército Soviético e chegou ao funk carioca há mais de duas décadas.

Oficialmente chamada "Solinho do Fora PT" , a música viralizou depois que Lucas Pavanato e Eduarda Campopiano (PL), eleitos deputado federal e deputada estadual por São Paulo, comemoraram a vitória dançando ao som dela. Depois, passou a tocar nos "bloquinhos do 22" e em comícios do então candidato à Presidência.

A melodia que acompanha versos contra a esquerda surgiu com uma letra que exalta o povo russo na década de 1860 e, após a revolução comunista de 1917, se tornou popular na URSS e foi cantada pelo coro do exército soviético.

Década de 1860 : surge na Rússia a partir do poema "Korobeiniki", de Nikolai Nekrasov, e vira canção popular

Década de 1980 : entra no repertório do coro do Exército Soviético, que grava a canção em show em Londres

1989 : vira o tema do Tetris na versão para Game Boy, com arranjo do japonês Hirokazu Tanaka

Início dos anos 2000 : a versão do Tetris chega ao funk carioca em montagens, e aparece em "Jonathan da Nova Geração", da Furacão 2000

2026 : a mesma melodia embala o funk do "petista disfarçado"

A melodia tem raiz antes mesmo da revolução comunista que deu origem à União Soviética. Conhecida como "Korobeiniki" ("mascates", em russo), a composição é baseada em um poema de Nikolai Nekrasov publicado em 1861, durante o Império Russo.

Nekrasov era conhecido por retratar a vida do povo russo. Os versos contam a história de um vendedor ambulante que se encontra com uma jovem. Com o passar do tempo, o poema ganhou uma versão musical e se popularizou como canção folclórica russa.

Capa da canção folclórica 'Korobeiniki'. — Foto: Reprodução/Wikimedia Commons

A canção entrou no repertório de grupos musicais do Exército Soviético, conhecidos no Ocidente como "Coro do Exército Vermelho". Um desses conjuntos a gravou ao vivo no Royal Albert Hall, em Londres, em março de 1988. O mesmo disco traz o hino britânico, árias de ópera e até "Yesterday", dos Beatles.

Não se trata, porém, de uma música militar ou revolucionária . Nos anos 1930, um musicólogo soviético chegou a lamentar que "Korobeiniki", cujo herói é um comerciante, fosse mais popular que as canções revolucionárias, segundo o jornal americano "The Boston Globe".

O Tetris foi criado em 1984 por Alexey Pajitnov, pesquisador da Academia de Ciências da União Soviética, em Moscou. A primeira versão do jogo, porém, não tinha som.

"Korobeiniki" virou o tema do Tetris em 1989, quando o compositor japonês Hirokazu Tanaka fez o arranjo para a versão do Game Boy, da Nintendo. Foi essa versão que ganhou o mundo.

Ou seja, a melodia que virou hit da direita brasileira ficou famosa graças a um jogo criado na União Soviética, ainda que no arranjo de um compositor japonês.

Funk do 'petista disfarçado', tocado em comícios da direita, tem base popularizada na União Soviética. — Foto: Reprodução

A melodia desembarcou no funk muito antes da campanha. Uma montagem musical com a melodia do Tetris era popular nos bailes cariocas. No início dos anos 2000, a Furacão 2000 inseriu a melodia "Jonathan da Nova Geração", cantada por Jonathan Costa, filho dos donos da equipe, quando ele tinha 7 anos.

A faixa combinava o tema do Tetris do Game Boy com o Volt Mix, batida criada em 1988 pelo DJ americano Battery Brain e muito usada no funk carioca dos anos 1990. Reaproveitar bases e trechos de músicas conhecidas é uma marca do gênero.

Em 2026, "Solinho do Fora PT" repetiu a combinação, com novos versos dirigidos ao PT e à esquerda.

Como o g1 mostrou, o funk virou trilha das campanhas da direita em 2026. Jingles no ritmo, com apoio a Flávio e críticas ao PT, embalaram atos e vídeos de nomes como Nikolas Ferreira, Lucas Pavanato e Eduarda Campopiano. No domingo do segundo turno, seis das 50 músicas mais ouvidas no país no Spotify eram desse tipo.

O uso foi alvo de críticas por contradição, já que políticos conservadores costumam associar os bailes funk à "narcocultura". Pavanato, que foi relator da CPI dos Pancadões na Câmara Municipal de São Paulo, diz que "o problema com o funk, por óbvio, é a letra, não o ritmo". A estratégia não atraiu grandes nomes do gênero: MCs como Hariel e PH apoiaram Lula, e outros ficaram neutros.

articles.title: Macklemore calls Free Palestine Tour his 'favourite thing' he has ever been part of
articles.summary: Rapper Macklemore shares heartfelt gratitude for the Free Palestine Tour, emphasizing collective voices and advocacy for Palestinian rights in London.
articles.body: Rapper Macklemore has expressed gratitude to the musicians, speakers and audiences who came together for the Free Palestine Tour in London, describing it as his "favourite thing" he has ever been part of.Macklemore, whose real name is Benjamin Hammond Haggerty, took to Instagram and said that the event reaffirmed the power of collective voices and platforms in advocating for Palestinian freedom, dignity and rights."The Free Palestine Tour is my favorite thing I've ever been a part of I am still overwhelmed with gratitude and awe for every musician who stepped on stage in London. Every speaker. Every person who chose to be there," Macklemore wrote in the caption section.He added: "We live in an era where advocating for Palestinian life and freedom is controversial. Where saying that Palestine should be free, that Palestinians deserve the same dignity, safety and rights as everyone else, can come at a cost."The rapper said that the tour served as a reaffirmation that "when we collectively use our voices, our stages and our platforms to stand for the freedom of others, something profound happens. And the crowd is just as much a part of that as the artists. We all are.""When we move beyond the fear of "how will this affect my career?" and center collective liberation, something shifts. Love is found. And that feeling of love was abundant in London. I can still feel it in my body."He further wrote: "After five of the most intense weeks, reaching out to artists, organizing, dealing with logistics and constant meetings, it felt like we could all finally exhale. There is so much work to do. The march is long. But this felt like a beautiful step toward rekindling something in all of our hearts.""Thank you to all the artists and speakers that said yes. And thank you to everyone that bought a ticket and supported. I feel honored to have shared that experience with you all. What a beautiful outcome."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: Diwali and the politics of gifting
articles.summary: It is that time of the year again when a subtle realisation occurs that gifting in NCR is no less than any competitive sport.
articles.body: It is that time of the year again when a subtle realisation occurs that gifting in NCR is no less than any competitive sport. Each year, you prepare in advance, armed with lessons from the last festive season, only to realise that there are more waiting for you this season. And no matter how well you think you know your friend circle, there are always surprises. Someone sends a luxury hamper, and suddenly your box of mithai or dry fruits looks inadequate. The bigger question isn’t what to gift, but how to match last year’s generosity without appearing either stingy or extravagant. Plus, there could be added pressure if you are known as someone who always sends a gift of a certain value. You go lower than that, friends and relatives might assume (and gossip) that you are broke. You spend more, and there might be questions raised about ‘where is all this money coming from?’ Clearly, there is no winning this game.A month before the festive season begins, a budget is earmarked for Diwali gifting. There are categories within that budget, as per the hierarchy of gifting – one for neighbours, friends and acquaintances, a slightly more personalised, better gift for close friends, and a premium range for business associates. And for some, there is an added category for those who unexpectedly turn up with a gift close to Diwali. Of course, the hierarchy isn’t always determined by how close you are to someone. There are people you meet once a year but cannot afford to leave out of your gifting list, and then there are friends who would be perfectly happy sharing a box of mithai with you. The tricky part is deciding who belongs where, because getting the category wrong could mean an entire year of awkwardness. And just when you think the lists have been finalised, budgets approved and gifts dispatched, someone who wasn’t even on your list sends you an elaborate hamper. Now, what should have been a pleasant surprise becomes a fresh problem. One option is to pick up something from the stack of gifts kept aside specifically for regifting. But the real dilemma arises when the gift you have received looks rather expensive and you have absolutely no intention of spending a similar amount on a return gesture. Do you send something modest and hope they don’t notice the difference? Do you make anexception and stretch your budget? Or do you simply thank them profusely and hope that gratitude counts as reciprocation?Then comes the rather delicate business of regifting. While most people have no qualms about passing on an unopened box of dry fruits or an elaborate festive hamper, one has to be extremely careful about where it came from and where it is headed. The last thing you want is for a gift to find its way back to the person who originally sent it.There is also the question of whether a gift needs to be personally delivered or whether sending it through a driver is enough. Does dropping it off at the gate count as a festive gesture? Should you call to check if it has been received? And if someone makes the effort to personally deliver a gift, are you now expected to return the favour with a visit? Suddenly, the gifting exercise begins to resemble the scheduling of Diwali parties, with lists, locations and social obligations to manage. Perhaps the most amusing part of this entire exercise is that while everyone insists that ‘it’s the thought that counts’, an extraordinary amount of thought goes into calculating the value of the gift, the relationship with the recipient and the possible consequences of getting either wrong. By the time Diwali arrives, you have spent so much time deciding on gifting that you begin to wonder whether festive gifting was ever meant to be this complicated.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Dwayne Johnson beams with pride as daughter honours Polynesian culture
articles.summary: Dwayne Johnson expresses pride for daughter Jazzy and Nonosina dancers as they celebrate Polynesian culture through dance at the Rose Bowl, performing in front of 33,000 spectators. Actor encourages youth to embrace cultural heritage and continue striving for greatness.
articles.body: Hollywood star Dwayne Johnson expressed pride in his daughter Jazzy and the dancers of Nonosina as they honoured Polynesian culture through their graceful storytelling movements in front of an audience of 33,000.Calling himself a proud father and "Uncle Rock" to the young performers, the actor took to Instagram and encouraged them to remain humble, hungry and keep reaching for more.Johnson wrote: "Very proud of my daughter, Jazzy and all of our @nonosina1965 dancers, upholding and honoring our Polynesian culture with their beautiful, and GRACEFUL storytelling movements at the @rosebowlstadium in front of 33,000 strong."The art is in our dance. The love is in our mana. Clearly I'm a very proud faced papa and "uncle Rock" to all these young ones - keep reaching for more, humble, hungry and every step along the way matters."He concluded: "Shout to @uclaathletics + @uclafootball for all the love - and stay undefeated and shout to the core lady bosses @tiana_nonosina @kay.faam @laurenhashianofficial for making it all happen with love, pride, discipline x Uncle Rock cheehooo."On the acting front, Johnson will next be seen in 'Jumanji: The Open World'. The upcoming installment will bring back Hart as Franklin Finbar, Johnson as Dr. Bravestone, Jack Black as Professor Sheldon Oberon and Karen Gillan as Ruby Roundhouse.Jumanji, first released in 1995, was directed by Joe Johnston and based on Chris Van Allsburg's 1981 children's picture book. The film is the first installment in the Jumanji film series and stars Robin Williams, Kirsten Dunst, David Alan Grier, Bonnie Hunt, Jonathan Hyde, and Bebe Neuwirth.Johnson is a semi-retired professional wrestler. articles.title: Mahjong finds a seat at the Diwali party table
articles.summary: What once used to be a popular social engagement among Indian army wives in cantonment towns has now made inroads in Delhi’s elite circle as its favourite
articles.body: What once used to be a popular social engagement among Indian army wives in cantonment towns has now made inroads in Delhi’s elite circle as its favourite party game. The popularity of Mahjong, a 19th century Chinese tile game, started making news last year. From then to now it has skyrocketed to an extent that Mahjong has acquired a high table at Diwali parties. The game’s social status and engagement score even seem to exceed the popularity of traditional games like Teen Patti at Diwali parties. Now, a setup or two for Mahjong with highly engrossed players has become a common sight at parties this festive season.‘Now most Diwali parties have a Mahjong setup or two’Fashion designer Ritu Beri, a proud Army kid who’s grown up watching her mother play Mahjong, shares that she is surprised at how the game, which she saw her mom playing all her life, has now become the talk of the town. “In the Army, it was the one game that everyone played, there was no Rummy or anything else, for army wives it was only Mahjong. I still remember my mom had the most beautiful ivory Mahjong set, a rare set. It is so nostalgic for me when someone says, ‘Let’s meet over Mahjong,’” she tells us.The ‘game of luck and strategy’ has been popular at theme parties, and we have been told that there is “hardly any upscale kitty party that doesn’t have Mahjong.” Given its popularity, it is understandable when we are told that Karwa Chauth Mahjong events and parties were a hit this festive season.“I do Mahjong events and parties with my friends regularly and it was one of the most appropriate fit for a Karwa Chauth gathering. This game keeps you engrossed, you actually can spend hours playing it. Once you start playing, it gets so interesting that you lose track of time. Now most Delhi parties have Mahjong setups and it is as popular as card games, even more,” says Sunayana Bhinder Chibba, who has been organising Mahjong parties for her friends.‘Mahjong is replacing games like Rummy and Teen Patti’Along with parties, there are also festive events being organised by Mahjong-exclusive clubs with hundreds of members across cities. The growing interest has also turned Mahjong into a reason to host a party rather than just as an activity. From private sessions among friends to larger gatherings organised by clubs, the game has acquired a social calendar of its own. Mumbai-based Ria Bajaj, co-founder of The Mahjong Network, shares, “Ever since the beginning of the festive season, we have been flooded with queries to arrange Mahjong events and private parties. We have an event or a party happening every two days in the city and requests are still pouring in.”And while Mahjong may have traditionally been associated with women’s social gatherings, its growing popularity is now drawing interest from everyone. So much so that even restaurants are looking to cash in on the trend by adding Mahjong to their festive celebrations. Maneka Jain Daswani, Ria’s partner and co-founder of The Mahjong Network based in Delhi, adds, “This festive season Diwali card parties are being replaced by Mahjong parties as it is no longer a ladies’ game. It will be safe to say that Mahjong is fast replacing party games like Rummy or Teen Patti.”‘People are requesting crash courses for the game’The spike in Mahjong’s popularity has also led to many seeking crash courses for the game, especially in the festive season. Noida-based Mahjong coach from Indian Mahjong Association, Vineeta Sahni, who has been playing Mahjong for over three decades now and is also teaching the game now, says that she has been getting requests every day from people who want to learn Mahjong in a couple of hours. “Some people are only seeing this as a social engagement activity and to be a part of the circle, they are looking for crash courses, but the game is not learnt this way. We conduct sessions to introduce the game, provide tables and even train individuals who are interested in learning the game. We recommend a three-hour class to learn and I think five classes are essential. During the festive season, we are witnessing a demand for trainers by those hosting Mahjong parties,” says Vineeta.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Paris Jackson files new documents in court and demands USD 600 million from her father’s estate; she alleges money has been withheld from being given to her and her siblings
articles.summary: In a recent court filing, Paris Jackson has demanded $600 million from her father's estate, alleging that executors are withholding her inheritance. The legal battle highlights concerns about trust fund distributions intended for Michael Jackson's children.
articles.body: Paris Jackson has now demanded USD 600 million from her late father Michael Jackson’s estate. The case has been going on for years; however, in recent claims, the actress and singer has accused the longtime executors of his will of keeping his children from receiving their inheritance.Page Six reported that the 28-year-old filed a court case in the matter and has requested a judge to order the estate to make a distribution of the requested amount to the Michael Jackson Family Trust. She stated that there was no legitimate reason behind the ongoing delay in transferring the amount since her father’s passing almost 17 years ago.The report also states that Paris claimed that the trust, which had been intended to benefit her and her brothers, Prince, 29, and Bigi, 24, has remained unfunded, even though the estate has been making millions of dollars for years now and continues to do so. The filing was made to the Los Angeles Superior Court on October 29, directly targeting John Branca, who is the executor of her father’s estate. The filing stated that he has had an “iron grip” over the funds and controls how, when, and if the money is allocated to the pop singer’s children. According to her statements, her father’s will clearly stated that all of his children should have received their part from the trust after they turned 21; however, instead of following the instructions from the will, they have been given much smaller amounts determined by Branca.Paris Jackson alleges that the amount was further reduced after she sought legal aid last yearThe legal matter between Paris Jackson and the executors of her father’s estate has been going on since last year. She has made multiple allegations against them, which also include Branca providing “non-contractual gifts” to colleagues. Despite everything, her concerns and claims were not taken seriously; instead, they were met with dispute and discouragement. articles.title: Michael Jackson’s Daughter Seeks $600 Million From His Estate, Says Trust Remains Unfunded
articles.summary: Paris Jackson, the daughter of the late King of Pop Michael Jackson, petitioned a Los Angeles probate court to order a $600 million distribution from her fat...
articles.body:
Paris Jackson , the daughter of the late King of Pop Michael Jackson, petitioned a Los Angeles probate court to order a $600 million distribution from her father's estate to the Michael Jackson Family Trust, arguing that she and her brothers have waited more than 17 years for it to be funded.

In legal documents, obtained and viewed by TheWrap, Jackson claimed that her father always intended for his children, including brothers Prince and Bigi Jackson, to receive "income from the Trust on their respective twenty-first birthdays." However, as the document highlighted, "Those dates have all long passed."

"More than 17 years after his passing, Michael Jackson's family trust remains unfunded," the filing stated. "In 2011, Executors informed the Court they 'are contemplating and do intend to file a separate Petition for Preliminary Distribution.' Fifteen years later, Michael's beneficiaries are still waiting."

"Paris respectfully submits that the Estate's wealth is a testament to the singular talent and incredible work ethic of her father," the document continued. "That said, Executors' contributions to the Estate's liquidity, including the restructuring of debt, certain high-risk entertainment projects, and principally the selling off of assets, have produced considerable amounts of cash. Executors, however, have never presented any plan for funding the Michael Jackson Family Trust to the Court. That needs to change."

Later on in the filing, Jackson claimed that she and her siblings received "lesser amounts dictated by the remaining Executor, who use[d] this power to deter them from checking his abuses."

"Michael also intended for each sibling to begin receiving outright principal distributions from the Trust on their respective thirtieth birthdays," the document added. "That milestone is fast approaching. Prince turns 30 in four months, Paris turns 29 in April, and Bigi turns 25 in February."

Per the filing, Jackson's daughter raised "the unfunded trust as an issue a year ago" in a separate legal document, alleging that the executor had "failed to take action."

Jackson's legal team argued that her father's estate has generated a significant amount of money thanks to various business deals and property sales, including the sale of its interest in EMI Music Publishing, the sale of Neverland Ranch and a deal with Sony regarding the singer's music and IP assets. Her attorneys claimed that this fiscal reality made it possible for them to partially distribute funds to the family trust.

"Indeed, Paris is informed that, even when potential liabilities are taken into account, the Estate holds approximately $600 million in distributable cash, not to mention any cash that may be held at the entity level," the document claimed. "Any other concerns regarding outstanding liabilities can be handled through appropriate refunding agreements with the trustee and, if needed, the beneficiaries."

In response to the filing, the Michael Jackson Estate told People that it was unable fully fund the trusts in-questions until other legal matters were resolved, including litigation with the Internal Revenue Service, which sought $700 million in taxes and penalties from the estate.

"The Estate was able to secure a ruling to significantly reduce that amount, but the matter has not been settled and could still change," the late singer's estate said in a statement. The estate also slammed the claim that it was withholding or reducing payments to Jackson's beneficiaries as a "complete fabrication," adding, "None of his children receive a distribution until they are in their 30s."

articles.title: ‘Ramayana’: Makers reveals Hans Zimmer said, 'I don’t need to see it' before agreeing to compose music with AR Rahman
articles.summary: While Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s roles in ‘Ramayana’ remain a major talking point, the film is also drawing attention for a rare musical partnership between
articles.body: While Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s roles in ‘Ramayana’ remain a major talking point, the film is also drawing attention for a rare musical partnership between AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. In a new behind-the-scenes video, producer Namit Malhotra revealed that the Hollywood music composer came on board without even going through the film’s complete pitch deck.A glimpse into the making of the musicThe makers have released a video that shows AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer working side by side. Musicians from India and the West are seen coming together to build a symphony for the film. Talking about the project, Hans Zimmer said, “Together we are setting off on a journey that has never been done before, to be able to make music that is thousands of years old about the Gods and traditions that make India so important for us in the West.”Hans Zimmer did not need the pitch deckNamit Malhotra recalled meeting the Hollywood composer in New York with a presentation prepared on the film’s world and story. He said, “I met Hans in New York. I had made my entire pitch deck and all the world-building. I ran six or seven slides, and he said, ‘Namit, it is okay. I don’t need to see it.’” The producer also spoke about how artists from both sides of the world joined hands for the project.How AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer shared the workAR Rahman explained that the two composers split the work between them. He took charge of certain songs and themes, while Hans handled others, and they later merged everything together. According to him, the process involved a constant back-and-forth as they looked for what suited the film best.‘Such a blessing’, says AR RahmanIn an earlier conversation with Hindustan Times, AR Rahman called Hans’ presence on the film a blessing. He said, “Usually I prefer solo work because I’m bad at being precious about my work. I’d just say, ‘You do everything, and I’ll watch!’ But in this case, him coming onto the project is such a blessing because it changes the narrative. If someone in New Zealand or Europe sees Hans Zimmer’s name, they will watch. If they just see Indian names, they might think it’s just another Indian movie, but they’ll be curious to see what he has done collaborating on this. It’s a great move by the producer.”‘Ramayana’ release dateDirected by Nitesh Tiwari, ‘Ramayana’ will release in theatres on November 5.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ranbir Kapoor reacts to the mixed early reviews to 'Ramayana': 'Kuchh to log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna'
articles.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious adaptation of the Indian epic 'Ramayana' has remained in the spotlight ever since its first teaser was unveiled earlier this
articles.body: Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious adaptation of the Indian epic 'Ramayana' has remained in the spotlight ever since its first teaser was unveiled earlier this year. With the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer set to arrive in cinemas worldwide this Thursday, November 5, the film's lead actor and co-producer Namit Malhotra have finally addressed the months of trolling, memes and online criticism surrounding the project.During an interaction with students at an IIMUN event, Ranbir spoke about how he views the criticism directed at the film and said that one should not allow online reactions to affect them. The actor, who essays the role of Lord Rama, said, “What’s relevant today is this beauty of trolling online. It goes back to the good ol’ song ‘Kuchh to log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna'. I think that’s a great philosophy to actually follow in life. Don’t be bothered by what people are saying. What matters is the people who matter, the people who care for your work, your intention, and your kindness. That’s what matters the most,”Director Nitesh Tiwari also shared his perspective on the criticism, adding, “If your conscience is clear, and if our effort was hundred per cent, then what else do you need?”Interestingly, Ranbir's reference to the song 'Kuchh To Log Kahenge' also brings back memories of his 2018 film 'Sanju', directed by Rajkumar Hirani. In the biographical drama based on actor Sanjay Dutt's life, Ranbir's character is advised by his father, played by Sunil Dutt, to follow the philosophy of the song. Written by Anand Bakshi, the track featured in Shakti Samanta's 1972 romantic film 'Amar Prem'.Meanwhile, Namit Malhotra, who is backing the epic through Prime Focus, has also spoken about the social media reactions to 'Ramayana' in a recent international interview. Rather than letting the memes and criticism bother him, the producer said he has learnt to laugh along with them.“Honestly, after a point, I’ve started laughing at it because it’s meant for humour. All these people just want to have fun at someone’s expense. Today, it’s me. Tomorrow, it’ll be someone else. They just need someone in the news today to make fun of. The best in the world are getting trolled today. So, I just take it in the stride and enjoy it because how often do you get that opportunity?,” said Malhotra.The producer also pointed out that the film has received considerable appreciation alongside the negative reactions, and he is choosing to accept both. Drawing a parallel with Lord Rama's journey, he added, “As Lord Rama said famously in the film, if I was happy to take the crown, I’ll take exile with the same ease because that’s what life is, that’s what our destiny is. I’d have to take the good and the bad together, and that’s what you learn from it,”The film recently held its world premiere at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, California. With the international review embargo now lifted, early reactions have been mixed, with some critics praising its scale and visual spectacle while others have raised questions about its characterisation and execution.IndieWire offered a positive assessment of the film's elaborate storytelling and visual elements, writing, “There are enough wars, musical numbers, “Gladiator”-style arena contests, talking eagles, lavish Indian weddings, Shakespearean feuds, da Vinci-esque flying machines, and shape-shifting to satisfy even the most attention span-challenged viewers,”The publication further highlighted the film's numerous dramatic moments and its music, adding, “Ramayana contains dozens of moments that would each be the climax of another film. It seems like every single scene features someone learning their destiny, meeting their true love, succumbing to their worst temptation, or winning their toughest battle. And each moment is scored with appropriate musical majesty by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman, the former of which is lending his talents to an Indian film for the first time,”However, IGN was less impressed with the film's treatment of its central characters. Commenting on Ranbir Kapoor's Rama and Sai Pallavi's Sita, the review stated, “Much like Kapoor’s Rama, Pallavi’s Sita is graceful in posture, but there’s little underlying either of them as actual human beings,”It also criticised the action sequences and comic elements, adding, “The fantasy fights lack the necessary physical and emotional weight to make a lasting impact, even before Rama’s fellow exiled brother Lakshmana (Ravi Dubey) delivers his umpteenth comic quip met by awkward dead air, adding to the Marvel-ness of it all.”Screen Rant, meanwhile, praised the performances of Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi but felt that the characters could have been explored in greater depth. Its review stated, “Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi excel in the more action-packed moments, and do bring a lot of charm to the handful of scenes that expand on their characters. However, they (and most of the movie’s characters) are rooted so thoroughly in their embodiment of their mythological selves that they don’t always feel fully human. The exception to this is Yash as the antagonistic Ravana, who actually gets a fascinating focus in the film’s first act. Growing into a fearsome king whose dueling ideologies of revenge and restraint are embodied by avatars of himself within his mind, Ravana has the kind of clear personality that could have fleshed out the rest of the cast.”Apart from Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, the film features Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Yash as Ravana. The ensemble cast also includes Arun Govil as Dasharatha, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Sheeba Chaddha as Manthara, Kunal Kapoor as Indra, Shobana as Kaikesi, Rakul Preet Singh as Shurpanakha, Vivek Oberoi as Vidyuthjiva and Anupam Kher as Jatayu.Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, 'Ramayana' is co-produced by Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, with Namit Malhotra backing the ambitious cinematic adaptation.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Director Honey Trehan has strongly criticised the Central Board of Film Certification’s (CBFC) latest advisory for filmmakers.
articles.body: Director Honey Trehan has strongly criticised the Central Board of Film Certification’s (CBFC) latest advisory for filmmakers. The board issued the notice on October 26 and made it clear that announced titles and release dates will not be considered during certification. Honey, whose Diljit Dosanjh-starrer ‘Satluj’ (earlier titled ‘Panjab 95’) was denied certification, called the new rule ‘cowardness and dictatorship’.Honey Trehan reacts to the new advisoryNews of the advisory spread widely on Monday and drew mixed reactions. Honey shared a poster of ‘Satluj’ posted by Variety India on his Instagram Stories, with the text ‘New CBFC guidelines for filmmakers’ on it. Sharing his view, he wrote, “New Guidelines shows and underlines the cowardness & the dictatorship in the country, not the democratic approach towards the freedom of speech.”What the new CBFC advisory saysThe CBFC had issued guidelines for filmmakers in September, and the latest advisory followed in October. This year, 18 new members were named to the board, the first such change since 2017. Preity Zinta, Pankaj Tripathi, Suniel Shetty, Pallavi Joshi, Ricky Kej and Supriya Yarlagadda are part of the new panel. As per the advisory, makers must submit the final version of their film, with titles, graphics and sound, for certification. It also states that announced titles and release dates will not be taken into account.The long certification battle of ‘Satluj’Honey’s reaction comes after ‘Satluj’ remained stuck with the CBFC for almost three years. The makers and the board were in a standoff, as the makers did not agree to the changes the board asked for. The film, first titled ‘Ghallughara’, was later renamed ‘Panjab 95’. In July, it was quietly released without cuts on Zee5 as ‘Satluj’, but it was removed within hours.‘Jana Nayagan’ also faced delaysTamil Nadu chief minister Vijay’s last film, ‘Jana Nayagan’, also remained with the CBFC for months. It was sent to a revising committee at the last minute, just before its planned Pongal release in January. The makers went to court against the board but got no relief. The film finally reached theatres in July after the makers made the changes the board wanted. articles.title: Rebecca Gayheart details Eric Dane’s final week of life: ‘Had no idea that was it’
articles.summary: Rebecca Gayheart has opened up about the final days of husband Eric Dane’s life, from family sleepovers in his room to having “no idea that was it” during his last trip to the hospital.
articles.body: Rebecca Gayheart has opened up about the final days of husband Eric Dane’s life, from family sleepovers in his room to having “no idea that was it” during his last trip to the hospital. Dane died at 53 in February, less than one year after publicly announcing he had been diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Gayheart, 55, spoke with NBC special correspondent Maria Shriver on TODAY Nov. 3, the release day for Dane’s posthumous memoir, “My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments.” The actor shared how she and their two daughters “never, ever anticipated” that they would lose him in February. “He had gone to the hospital so many times before, and they would patch him up, so to speak, and he would come home,” Gayheart said. “And he’d be OK. And we’d go back to the normal routine, which did change week by week.” She recalled the first day of Dane’s final trip to the hospital. “I said, ‘Listen, I’ll be back. I have a dinner. I’m going to this event.’ I had no idea that that was it, that that week was going to be our last week,” Gayheart said. “And nor did my daughters. It really took a few days for us to understand the gravity of what that last trip to the hospital meant.” Gayheart and Dane married in 2004 and filed for divorce in 2018. Gayheart filed to have the divorce dismissed in 2025. They co-parented their daughters, and she was by his bedside in his final week. The actor and model and their daughters, Billie, 16, and Georgia, 14, began to realize the gravity of the situation after a couple of days. “I think it was like day three in the hospital where it shifted,” Gayheart said. “Everything shifted. Just the tone of when the doctors were talking to us, and some of the information we were given.” Dane also recognized how serious things were getting. “He was fully aware it was shifting, and he was still communicating with us,” Gayheart said. “Not well verbally, but I could understand him most of the time. The kids could most of the time, his closest friends.” Friends of the couple who are doctors helped Gayheart navigate that emotional time, during which she said she suffered from “decision fatigue.” She said Dane knew he was dying. “It was figuring it out as we went,” she said. “But I remember the moment Eric decided to make some choices, and he did. ... He was in control of the way he was going to leave.” To comfort the “Grey’s Anatomy” and “Euphoria” actor in his final days, Gayheart and their daughters conducted their usual family sleepover in Dane’s hospital room. “The girls and I just camped out there with him, and we had our family sleepovers,” she said. “And we brought in those little candles that aren’t real candles. They have batteries. And we played his favorite music, and we tried to make it as nice as you can be in the hospital room.” Gayheart was unprepared for how swiftly the end came. “A lot of people will say, ‘Well, at least you knew, and you could have those last conversations,’” she said. “But we didn’t know, because there is no road map. No one can tell you what the journey looks like because it’s so different for every patient. “He was becoming more alive mentally, but losing all of his physical abilities. And for the girls, that was really hard to watch as well. But overall, it’s a blur, because it was just so overwhelming.” In the wide-ranging conversation, Gayheart also spoke to Shriver about Dane’s posthumous book, his decision to go public about his ALS diagnosis, her struggles in becoming a caregiver, the moment she found out he had ALS and how their daughters are faring in the wake of his death. “He became a different person in a way,” Gayheart said. “He really valued his life suddenly, and every minute of how he was going to spend his life and what he was going to do with his days.”

articles.title: Adobe’s Premiere mobile app is adding licensed music from ‘leading artists’
articles.summary: Adobe is teaming up with Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group to add a library of licensed music clips to the Premiere mobile video editing app.﻿
articles.body: Adobe is teaming up with Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group to add a library of licensed music clips to the Premiere mobile video editing app. No specific musicians have been announced with this partnership, but Adobe said it will include “popular songs” from “leading artists,” and enable Premiere mobile users to quickly jump on “the latest trend.” “By bringing licensed music from UMG artists into Adobe Premiere mobile, we’re giving creators new ways to build their stories around the songs they love for the first time, while helping our artists and songwriters reach new audiences,” Universal Music Group’s Bryan Stone said in the announcement. Adobe says this feature is “coming soon,” and will allow Premiere mobile users to: * Add up to 60 seconds of a popular track directly to the video. * Browse, search and preview trending music by artist or track, filter by genre and duration, bookmark favorites, and explore popular music through label-featured collections. * Access customizable templates that are already paired with music to speed up editing. * Export finished videos in Premiere mobile and post to licensed social platforms. The Premiere Pro desktop app and Premiere mobile both already include a built-in library of royalty-free music that editors can work into their videos, but licensed audio needs to be manually imported. This update aims to make it easier to incorporate recognizable music into video edits, and help Adobe’s mobile video editor compete against popular rivals like CapCut. We have asked Adobe if these updates will also be coming to Premiere Pro, and will update if we hear back.

articles.title: Celebrity loses injunction bid but will stay anonymous pending appeal
articles.summary: The unnamed man asked for an injunction to stop his identity being reported in connection with allegations against him.
articles.body:
A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the court saying the man's claim for an injunction was denied.

But the judge Mr Justice Nicklin said a temporary injunction preventing the man from being named and the allegations published should remain in place, in order to allow the celebrity to appeal against the judgment, with anonymity and reporting restrictions remaining in force during the period allowed for any appeal.

ITN and the Guardian have said they believe it is in the public interest to publish allegations that the man abused his status to attempt or attempt to engage in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".

The man, who denies the allegations, said any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself, and that the court should prevent any publication or broadcast.

In a judgment on Tuesday, Nicklin rejected the injunction request and said in a summary of his ruling: "The claimant's claim for an injunction was dismissed.

"The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make."

He added that the man will remain anonymous to allow any appeal to be lodged.

During a two-day trial last week, the court heard that the man denies abusing "his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them".

The celebrity's lawyers told the court that his high suicide risk was not because of any wrongdoing, but because of the fear of "trial by media".

Sara Mansoori KC, representing the man, told the court that any publication "would have a potentially fatal impact".

The barrister told the court: "The only reason they would not be fatal is because the claimant would be locked up and prevented from his desire to end his life."

She said the man had made a suicide attempt after receiving letters from ITN and Guardian News and Media (GNM) asking for his response to the allegations, and later absconded from hospital and attempted suicide for a second time.

She added in written submissions: "This is not a case where an individual has spuriously raised 'mental health' concerns in the face of an impending publication that they do not wish to occur.

"The claimant has attempted suicide twice as a result of these matters, been hospitalised for months, been the subject of involuntary detention and been examined by multiple - now more than 10 - doctors."

Mansoori also said the man "has no intention of returning to public life".

Gavin Millar KC, for ITN and GNM, said in written submissions that "numerous allegations" had been gathered during "a wide-ranging and rigorous investigation" and that there was a "strong" public interest in publishing them.

He said reporters had spoken to more than 100 people, and that the resulting allegations "indicated a pattern of behaviour".

Millar later said many of the women "have been traumatised by the claimant's alleged conduct and have suffered mental health crises and mental illness as a result".

He argued that while the state may have a responsibility to protect life, applying that principle to this case would require the state to intervene in "lawful journalistic activities" to prevent "an autonomous act by the claimant himself".

A medical report carried out for the court said inpatient treatment could provide "significant, but not complete mitigation of the risk", but that treatment, perhaps for months, had "a realistic potential to reduce the risk".

The BBC Action Line website has information about organisations that can offer support for the issues raised in this story.

articles.body: Fans were in for a surprise when international singer Ed Sheeran’s voice turned up in a Shah Rukh Khan film song. Now, the singer has explained how it all came together. ‘Tu Mil Jaaye’, the first track from Shah Rukh’s upcoming film ‘King’, features Ed along with Arijit Singh and Madhubanti Bagchi.Ed Sheeran shares the story behind the songIn an Instagram post on Tuesday evening, Ed wrote, “When I first met Shah Rukh, he said I must make a song to be in his next movie and also be my first Bollywood song. We’ve got to know each other over the years, and I love him. Last time I was in India, I went to his house to get him to shoot a cameo in the Sapphire music video for me and @arijitsingh. He introduced me to @sachinjigar that day, and I wrote and recorded my verse for Tu Mil Jaaye for his movie King that night. I love that Arijit is singing on it with me too, all my favourite people on one project. King is out December 24th, and Tu Mil Jaaye is out everywhere now.”Ed Sheeran’s Mannat visitShah Rukh Khan and his family had welcomed the singer at their Mumbai home, Mannat, in March 2024, when Ed was visiting India.About ‘King’Directed by Siddharth Anand, ‘King’ is set to hit theatres on December 24, 2026. ‘Tu Mil Jaaye’, the first official release from the film, hints that the movie will be a dark thriller. Apart from Shah Rukh Khan, the cast includes his daughter Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, Deepika Padukone, Arshad Warsi and Rani Mukerji. The cast also includes Anil Kapoor, Jaideep Ahlawat, Jackie Shroff, Raghav Juyal, and Abhay Verma.Suhana Khan is set to make her big-screen debut with the film. articles.title: In 2022, Jennifer Lopez became nonprofit microloan provider’s ambassador: years later, it reported $8 billion in loans and 291,602 small businesses helped with an aim to reach 750,000 entrepreneurs by the next decade
articles.summary: Jennifer Lopez's partnership with Grameen America has resulted in $8 billion in microloans to help over 291,602 women-owned small businesses thrive, aiming for 750,000 entrepreneurs by 2030.
articles.body: When Jennifer Lopez joined a microfinance nonprofit in 2022 as National Ambassador, she did so with the main goal of championing financial equity and elevating Latina entrepreneurs who often tend to face steep barriers in mainstream banking. Today, that collaboration has helped propel the non-profit to $8 billion in total loan capital disbursed, proving that community trust and affordable microcapital can drive generational wealth creation.What is Grameen America?According to its website, it is a non-profit microfinance organization that was founded in 2008 by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus. The main aim of the organization is to help low-income, entrepreneurial women build small businesses to achieve financial mobility and lift themselves and their families out of poverty.Jennifer Lopez became an ambassador for the nonprofit microfinance organizationIn 2022, the beloved actress, singer, and philanthropist joined the organization as one of their main brand ambassadors in order to promote microloans and local business growth among Latina women.One of the major achievements of the organization is that, according to their platform, it recorded USD 8 billion disbursed in affordable small business microloans to thousands of people. The help was focused on 291,602 small businesses, which were primarily women-owned enterprises living below or near the federal poverty line. The campaign that Lopez was a part of was an expansion campaign. It was a five-year initiative backed by USD 600 million in new fundraising, combining philanthropy and debt capital, to fuel an estimated USD 1 billion program expansion. The campaign is still going, with the main target set on deploying USD 40 billion in capital and reaching 750,000 entrepreneurs over the next decade.How they worked on providing such microloans?One of the main ways these microloans worked was through a trust-based, peer-to-peer system where borrowers form small peer networks, and members support and encourage one another rather than needing corporate collateral, balance sheets, or high credit scores. The organization itself reports on-time loan repayments directly to credit bureaus, which in turn are helping low-income women establish formal credit histories and gain access to mainstream financial services over time. Lastly, beyond all of the capital, members receive ongoing financial education, peer networking, and mentorship—amplified through Lopez's advocacy—to transition from basic financial stability to long-term economic mobility.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: John Rich says Kathy Hochul is ‘running over’ NY farmers with renewable energy agenda
articles.summary: John Rich's country song "Dear Kathy" takes aim at Governor Kathy Hochul over renewable energy policies he says are silencing upstate New York farmers.
articles.body: John Rich is blasting New York Gov. Kathy Hochul over the state’s renewable energy policies, accusing her administration of silencing farmers and overriding local officials in upstate New York. The 52-year-old Big & Rich member has publicly joined local landowners, activists and officials who are challenging New York’s Office of Renewable Energy Siting (ORES), a state agency that reviews and permits major renewable energy and transmission projects. Last month, Rich released his new country song "Dear Kathy," which is directed at the Democratic governor, who is running for re-election. In the song, Rich speaks on behalf of farmers and landowners who are protesting large-scale solar and wind projects on upstate New York farmland, arguing that ORES has undermined local control and put family farms, rural communities and private property rights at risk. JOHN RICH WARNS NASHVILLE'S FAMED BROADWAY COULD GO DARK AS BUSINESSES FACE TAX ‘DEATH NAIL’ During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Rich shared his message for Hochul, pointing to the final line of "Dear Kathy," which asks, "Why do you hate these people so much?" "What have they ever done to you except pay taxes and put food on your table? That’s it," Rich said. "Why do you hate these people?" he continued. "Because only somebody that has a vindictive spirit would do what she’s doing to them — or greed." "I think greed is probably the largest driver in it because these companies that are coming in, building these huge fields. Listen, if you add up all the plans they have coming into upstate New York, it’s over 100 square miles of solar panels," Rich added. WILLIE NELSON URGES AMERICANS TO FIGHT 'WATER THIEVING' AI DATA CENTERS DEVOURING RURAL TEXAS FARMLAND The conflict centers on New York’s centralized permitting system for large-scale solar and wind projects. Created in 2020 under former Gov. Andrew Cuomo, ORES generally handles renewable energy projects capable of producing 25 megawatts or more. Its rules encourage developers to avoid the state’s most productive agricultural soils and require them to minimize or mitigate impacts when farmland cannot be avoided. ORES can also waive local zoning and land-use restrictions it deems "unreasonably burdensome," a power that critics argue gives state officials too much control over farmland and leaves local communities with limited say over projects in their areas. BROOKE ROLLINS, MONICA CROWLEY: AMERICA’S FAMILY FARMS HAVE KEPT US STRONG FOR 250 YEARS While speaking with Fox News Digital, Rich claimed Hochul’s administration used research from Cornell University to change how prime farmland is defined. The singer argued that the move made it easier for solar and wind projects to be built on agricultural land. WATCH: JOHN RICH SLAMS KATHY HOCHUL OVER FARMLAND DISPUTE: ‘WHY DO YOU HATE THESE PEOPLE?’ "She decided she didn’t like their definition of prime farmland because if it’s prime, it’s protected from solar and wind and projects like that," Rich said. "So they just redefined it. They just came up with a whole new equation and determined, well, based on these new numbers, there’s really no such thing as prime farmland anymore in upstate New York. So we can do whatever the hell we want to these people." AMISH FACE NEW YORK VACCINE MANDATE IN SUPREME COURT FIGHT, MIGHT HAVE TO ‘PACK THEIR WAGONS’ "Oh, by the way, we put ORES in place. So if they try to stop us, we just run right over the top of them," he continued. "I mean, it is a complete and total chokeout that she’s put on these farmers up there." "Some of these families have owned their farms, been in their families since before the Revolutionary War," Rich said. "You’re talking about one of the original 13 colonies, New York, and to think that 250 years later, after these same people’s ancestors had to fight off the British, now they’re standing there fighting with their own governor in the United States of America." "It is astonishing, and I find it to be disgusting. I also think it’s probably unconstitutional," he added. Since taking office in 2021, Hochul has continued to advance New York’s renewable energy agenda. Her administration has promoted large-scale solar and wind development and defended the state’s approach to farmland, arguing that renewable energy projects are not taking over New York’s "best farmland" and that leasing land for solar can help farmers keep their property in their families. When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, Hochul’s office pushed back on Rich’s criticism. "If he really wants to help farmers, maybe he can write a song calling on his buddy Donald Trump to lift the tariffs, end his reckless war with Iran that is driving up gas and diesel prices, and rein in the ICE raids, all of which are hurting farmers here in New York and across the country," Ken Lovett, a senior communications adviser on energy and environment for Hochul, said. DEBRA MESSING DITCHES DEMOCRAT FOR TRUMP-BACKED REPUBLICAN AS SHE SOUNDS ALARM OVER NEW YORK Rich said he first learned about the dispute after seeing Alexandra Fasulo, an upstate New York landowner and ORES critic, discuss it on social media. The singer said he was startled by the claim that the state could sideline landowners, zoning boards, mayors and other local officials when deciding where major projects would be built. "I said, that can’t be the case. I’m gonna go up and see this for myself," Rich recalled. Rich argued that ORES' authority undermines "home rule," the principle that landowners and local governments should have authority over how land in their communities is used. During his visit, Rich held two town hall meetings, including one at Fasulo’s farm, where he met with hundreds of farmers and landowners. "We had Amish people standing in the room being silent, standing in the back," Rich said. "It looked like something out of a movie." "And we had this discussion about ‘What are we going to do about this governor running over everybody?’" he continued. "And man, the sentiment in the room was so much frustration and feeling of bewilderment that what do you do? I mean, she's put something into gear here that just runs us over and takes away our voice." The singer told Fox News Digital that the meetings ultimately inspired him to write "Dear Kathy." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I left there thinking to myself, I need to put this song out, ‘Dear Kathy,’" he recalled. "I need to write a song for the governor of New York on behalf of all those people whose voices she has silenced. And so that led to me with a pencil and a piece of paper and a guitar writing a letter or a song to Kathy Hochul." WATCH: JOHN RICH SAYS MEETING AMISH FARMERS INSPIRED SONG TARGETING KATHY HOCHUL On Oct. 28, Rich officially released the song and its accompanying music video, which highlights affected areas in upstate New York, showcasing local landowners and the Holy Trinity Monastery in Jordanville, NY, which has actively opposed large wind projects near its grounds. "And I jokingly say in the video, 'What do you get the woman who has everything, including your freedom in her back pocket? Well, you give her the one thing she doesn't have — a country song,'" Rich said. "And so I wrote ‘Dear Kathy’ and it really was my way of speaking on behalf of those people that she will not listen to." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Rich described "Dear Kathy" as a "fight song" for the farmers he met and emphasized that the dispute transcended party lines. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE WATCH: JOHN RICH CALLS ‘DEAR KATHY’ A ‘FIGHT SONG’ FOR NEW YORK FARMERS "One interesting thing about those farmers that I met — they were Democrat, Republican, probably more Democrat than Republican, actually," he said. "And so it's not a partisan thing. Owning land is an American thing. I mean it may be one of the last things we all agree on in this country is that if you own land, if you bought that land, and you take care of that land, that's your land." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You get to determine what happens to it or what doesn't happen to it," he continued. "And that's exactly what I felt up there. It was an across the board repudiation of Kathy Hochul and her assault on their land and on them and on their legacies." "To me, as bad as that is, that was a beautiful experience actually for me to sit up there knowing that this is not a partisan deal, and I'm sitting in the room with both sides of the aisle, but everybody is in unison," Rich added. Despite his criticism of Hochul, Rich told Fox News Digital that he would welcome the opportunity to meet with Hochul to discuss the landowners’ concerns directly. "If Kathy Hochul wanted to sit with me and have a meeting, I would jump on the next thing smoking to be up there," he said. "I mean, I would sit down at her desk. She could bring anybody she wants and I would just ask questions. ‘Why do you think this is OK? I mean you're still an American. Don't you think that this is against the Constitution? Home rule is a real thing. You don't think that people that you govern have the right to determine what happens to their own land and not just a farm here or there, a hundred square miles of land?' I would just ask her basic questions."

articles.title: ‘Country Money’ singer Nicole Taylor of the trio Taylor Red passes away at 35: Triplet sisters Nika and Natalie say, 'She's healed in heaven' after her battle with breast cancer
articles.summary: Nicole Taylor, a member of the country music trio Taylor Red, has passed away at the age of 35.
articles.body: Nicole Taylor, a member of the country music trio Taylor Red, has passed away at the age of 35. Her triplet sisters, Nika Taylor and Natalie Taylor, shared the sad news in a TikTok video on Monday, November 2, and also spoke about her long fight with breast cancer.Sisters announce Nicole Taylor’s deathThe sisters said they were “heartbroken” over the loss. Nika said, “We’re heartbroken to announce the passing of our sister Nicole Taylor. We honestly thought she’d be healed here on earth, but now she’s healed in heaven.”Nicole Taylor’s cancer journeyAccording to the sisters, Nicole Taylor was diagnosed with stage three breast cancer in 2022. Natalie described it as an aggressive type and recalled how Nicole faced it. She said, “It was an aggressive type. In her words, when she first found out, was ‘God’s gonna use this for his glory.’ She thought it fearlessly, and she said, ‘We’re not going to live in dread during all of this.’ And she even did CrossFit while she was with her chemo treatments. She responded well to treatments and she was declared evidence without disease.”Natalie added, “Then after that she was told it turned into stage four. She tried not to live in fear, remained really hopeful. She travelled, she tried to live life, she worked really hard, she tried to have fun.”The sisters shared that Nicole was told “nine months later” that the cancer had returned as stage four and that she had “around three months to live.” Nika said, “[The doctor said] if the treatments worked, they didn’t know how long after that.”‘A big shock’ for the familyIn an emotional YouTube video posted on Monday, the sisters said the terminal diagnosis came as “a big shock.” Natalie said through tears, “We’re still processing everything. This, honestly, feels really hard to talk about, but we’re going to do our best to share her story.”Faith that gave her strengthThe sisters also played a clip of Nicole in her 20s speaking about her faith in God, which they said helped her through the illness. They shared that she “lived around a year after that prognosis” and tried to live as normally as possible. Nika said, “During the time of the more extreme diagnosis, we felt led to not live in fear and claim healing.”Natalie said, “She said she had so much peace and we’re really thankful for that. We are still shocked and didn’t think this would happen, but we know she’s not suffering anymore.”About Taylor RedThe country music trio is best known for the songs ‘Country Money’ and ‘Rent Free’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Johnny Depp no longer rules out a 'Pirates of the Caribbean' return after years away from franchise
articles.summary: Johnny Depp told Entertainment Tonight he's open to reprising Captain Jack Sparrow if Jerry Bruckheimer is involved and the sendoff is right.
articles.body: Johnny Depp isn't shutting the door on a return to the "Pirates of the Caribbean" franchise. "Pirates of the Caribbean" is one of the most successful franchises in Hollywood history. The first film — "Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl" — was released in 2003 and ushered in a new era of superstardom for Depp. It also launched the A-list careers of Kiera Knightley and Orlando Bloom. Four more films were released between 2006 and 2017 with Depp always reprising his role of Captain Jack Sparrow. TOM CRUISE IS REPORTEDLY GOING TO MAKE AN INSANE AMOUNT OF MONEY FOR TOP GUN 3 However, the franchise never returned past 2017 following the fallout between Johnny Depp and his ex-wife, Amber Heard, who he famously and successfully sued for defamation over abuse allegations published in the Washington Post. Johnny Depp doesn't rule out 'Pirates of the Caribbean' return Depp previously said there wasn't anything that could convince him to return to the franchise after the fallout. Now, it sounds like he's changing his tune and is open to reprising his role as Jack Sparrow if the situation is right. "If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the 'Pirates.' The only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note," Depp told Entertainment Tonight in a video published Monday. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER He continued, "I'll go to work with [producer Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything, you know. Doesn't matter. If it's Jerry, I trust him and we have deep friendship." You can watch his full comments in the video below, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com. "Pirates of the Caribbean" at its best — certainly the original film — is what great cinema is at its finest. It's fun, original, entertaining and doesn't take itself too seriously. There's also no preachy woke nonsense. Granted, that garbage didn't really exist in 2003. While it's very unclear if Depp will ever return to the "Pirates" universe, he has plenty of other things going on as he builds his career back up. He starred in "Jeanne du Barry" in 2023 and is starring in "Ebenezer," set for release Nov. 13, 2026, and "Day Drinker," scheduled for release in 2027. Both of his upcoming releases are major productions with stacked casts. articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: MCOCA court sends 13th accused Suneha Pandit, sister-in-law of gangster Anil Pandit, to police custody till November 16
articles.summary: A special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court in Mumbai on Tuesday sent Suneha Pandit, the 13th accused in the firing incident
articles.body: A special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court in Mumbai on Tuesday sent Suneha Pandit, the 13th accused in the firing incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff, to police custody till November 16. She is the sister-in-law of gangster Anil Pandit, who had claimed responsibility for the October 18 firing.Suneha Pandit arrested in Karnal in Tiger Shroff firing caseAccording to the IANS report, the Mumbai Crime Branch arrested Suneha Pandit from Haryana’s Karnal district. She was presented before the special MCOCA court on Tuesday, where investigators asked for her custody for further questioning. The police had sought 15 days of custody.Cryptocurrency account under the scannerOfficials said Suneha Pandit is the wife of Abhishek, who allegedly operates a cryptocurrency account. Money has reportedly come into this account from abroad, and investigators suspect it may be proceeds of extortion.Abhishek Pandit is the brother of Anil Pandit. He is accused of running two other groups along with his own network and is said to handle payments for all operations. Police said the other accused in the case were given special codes, which Abhishek allegedly used to transfer money to them.Defence opposes custodySuneha Pandit’s lawyer opposed the custody request, arguing that the police have already obtained all the information they needed. The Crime Branch, however, told the court that the funds allegedly used in the Tiger Shroff firing case came from foreign sources. The court then sent her to the custody of the Mumbai Crime Branch until November 16.Earlier arrests in the caseLast week, a special MCOCA court sent Amar, the 12th accused, to police custody till November 6. He was arrested in Rohna village in Haryana’s Sonipat. Officials said he allegedly transferred money online that was used in the crime, including for buying a motorcycle and booking hotel rooms linked to the case.Before that, the court had sent 11 other accused arrested in connection with the firing on Shroff’s car to police custody till November 6.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Identify school dropouts from minority communities, DC directs officials
articles.summary: Mandya DC Kumara directs officials to identify minority community school dropouts working in garages and bring them back to education under PM’s 15-point programme.
articles.body: Mandya: Deputy commissioner Kumara has directed officials to identify children from minority communities who have dropped out of school due to economic or social reasons and are working in garages and other establishments, and take steps to bring them back into the education system.Chairing a review meeting on the implementation of the Prime Minister’s new 15-point programme for minorities on Tuesday, he stressed the need for coordinated efforts to prevent children from being deprived of education. He instructed officials to identify students who remain continuously absent from school and ascertain the reasons for their absence.Children below 18 found working in garages must be identified and rehabilitated through coordinated efforts by the departments concerned.MLA appeals to youth to nurture talentMandya MLA Ravikumar P has called upon youngsters to identify and nurture their talents, participate in competitions and bring laurels at state and national levels.Speaking after inaugurating the District-Level Youth Festival 2026-27 at Sri Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar Kalamandira in Mandya on Tuesday, he said the festival provided an excellent platform for young people to showcase their abilities and gain recognition.Zilla panchayat CEO KR Nandini said more than 65% of India’s population comprised young people and urged them to set clear goals, recognise their individual strengths, work hard and stay away from bad habits.Pre-university education department deputy director Prasanna Kumar was present.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mysuru | Silver Rate in Mysuru | Bank Holidays in Mysuru | Public Holidays in MysuruStay updated with the latest Mysuru news.
